---
applyTo: "spec/jobs/**/*.rb,spec/features/**/*.rb"
---

# Job specs

- Test a job like a request spec: run it with `perform_now` and check its effects, e.g. the records it changes, the emails it sends, the jobs it enqueues and the requests it makes. You MUST NOT stub the models, actions, services or other classes the job calls, e.g. `allow(NewsletterClient).to receive(:new)` or `allow(Posts::ArchivePost).to receive(:call)`. To test how the job handles an action's `Error`, set up records that make the action fail for real.
- In job specs, you MUST NOT test an action's argument checks, e.g. that `Posts::PublishPost` raises `ActiveModel::ValidationError` for a post with unsaved changes from `unmodified:`.
- In job specs, name the `describe` block after the method the spec calls, e.g. `describe ".perform_now"`, not `describe "#perform"`.
- In job specs, stub only the HTTP requests the job makes to other services, and assert that it made them, with the service's stub helpers from `spec/support`, e.g. `newsletter_request = stub_newsletter_create` then `expect(newsletter_request).to have_been_requested`. When a service's SDK has its own stubs, use them instead, e.g. `stub_responses` in the AWS SDK.
- In job specs, in a `describe ".perform_later"` block, test each declaration the job has that changes what `perform_later` does: `queue_as`, `discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError` and `enqueue_after_transaction_commit`. Put everything the job does when it runs in `describe ".perform_now"`, e.g. the request `NotifySubscribersJob` makes to the newsletter service.
- In job specs, test `retry_on`, `rescue_from` and any other `discard_on` in `.perform_now`, because they act when the job runs, e.g. check that a `retry_on` job is enqueued again with `have_enqueued_job(described_class)`.
- In job specs, you SHOULD NOT check the job's arguments in `.perform_later`, because no declaration changes them and the request spec checks them.
- In `.perform_later`, build records with `build_stubbed` when the example doesn't run the job from the queue, e.g. `post = build_stubbed(:post)` for the queue and transaction checks.
- In job specs, check that the job is enqueued on the queue its `queue_as` names, e.g. `expect { described_class.perform_later(post) }.to have_enqueued_job(described_class).on_queue("default")`. When `queue_as` takes a block, write one example for each queue it can pick, e.g. `"enqueues news posts on the high queue"` and `"enqueues other posts on the default queue"`.
- When a job has `discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError`, test it in `.perform_later`: enqueue the job, delete the record, then run the queue with `perform_enqueued_jobs`, and check that it doesn't raise and does none of its work, e.g. `described_class.perform_later(post)`, `post.destroy!`, `expect { perform_enqueued_jobs }.not_to raise_error` and `expect(newsletter_request).not_to have_been_requested`. Check the work the job would otherwise do, so the example fails if the job runs. When the job waits for the commit, check `expect(described_class).to have_been_enqueued` before you delete the record. Use `create`, not `build_stubbed`, because a stubbed record is never saved and the example would pass without testing anything. You MUST NOT use `perform_now` for this.
- When a job sets `self.enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true`, check in `.perform_later` that it waits for the transaction to commit, e.g. `expect(described_class).not_to have_been_enqueued` inside `ActiveRecord::Base.transaction` and `.to have_enqueued_job(described_class)` on the block. Check that it isn't enqueued when the transaction rolls back, e.g. `raise ActiveRecord::Rollback` in the transaction and `.not_to have_enqueued_job(described_class)`. You SHOULD NOT write either check for a job that enqueues at once, because a rolled-back transaction doesn't remove it from the queue.
- When a job has a class method that enqueues it, test it in a `describe` block named after the method, e.g. `describe ".perform_later_for"`, and check the time it works out, e.g. `expect { described_class.perform_later_for(post) }.to have_enqueued_job(described_class).at(publish_at)` with `post = build_stubbed(:post, publish_at:)`.
- Cover every path through a scheduled job in its job spec, e.g. the drafts `PurgeAbandonedDraftsJob` deletes and the posts it keeps. You MUST NOT write a spec for the rake task.
- Run every job in at least one feature spec, so the spec checks that the app enqueues it and the persona gets the result.
- In feature specs, wrap the step that enqueues a job in `perform_enqueued_jobs`, and check for the success message inside the block, so the block waits for the request to finish and runs any jobs those jobs enqueue, e.g. `perform_enqueued_jobs { click_button "Publish"; expect(page).to have_css(".notice", text: "Post was published.") }`.
- Write a feature spec for every scheduled or maintenance job too. Name the feature after the task and start the scenario name with the persona who sees the result, e.g. `RSpec.feature "Draft Cleanup"` with `scenario "Author no longer sees abandoned drafts"`. Run the job with `perform_now` inside `perform_enqueued_jobs` in a `# WHEN` step, so any jobs it enqueues also run, e.g. `# WHEN the draft cleanup runs` then `perform_enqueued_jobs { PurgeAbandonedDraftsJob.perform_now }`, then check what the persona sees.
